docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
A Utility is a page, resource, or lookup kept for regular use at the table without being a rule.

Utilities are held to no style convention and follow no shared form. Each one is shaped by whatever it does, and they have nothing in common but being useful often enough to keep close at hand.

docs.title: Dark Elf Names
docs.text: Dark elves prefer names that flow off the tongue, though theirs carry a harsher sound.

docs.title: Elf Names
docs.text: Elves prefer names that flow off the tongue like wind through the trees.

docs.title: Bastions
docs.text: A Bastion is a character's own stronghold, a home base they build up and put to work between adventures.

docs.title: Gaining a Bastion
docs.text:
Bastions are awarded to individual players. You typically receive your Bastion around Character Level 5. Multiple player's Bastions can be combined into shared structures, or kept independent from one another.

You, the rest of your party, and the DM decide how your Bastions come into your possession. Their shape, style, and function are yours to decide.

docs.title: Bastion Facilities
docs.text: Every Bastion has Facilities: Basic Facilities that serve everyday needs, and Special Facilities for specific tasks.

docs.title: Facility Size
docs.text:
A Facility's Size is its area in 5-foot squares. That area can spread across multiple levels, as long as they are all connected.

Size Minimum Maximum Cramped 2 squares 4 squares Roomy 4 squares 16 squares Vast 16 squares 36 squares

docs.title: Basic Facilities
docs.text: A Basic Facility has no explicit effects, but makes a Bastion more comfortable to inhabit. A Basic Facility can resemble a Special Facility, but doesn't grant its effects. Each Bastion starts with one Cramped and one Roomy Basic Facility.

docs.title: Adding Basic Facilities
docs.text:
You can add new Basic Facilities or enlarge existing ones by spending money. The completed facility is available the next Day — paying the cost completes efforts that a Bastion's Hirelings have undertaken in the background.

Upgrading a Basic Facility increases its Size and costs the difference between its current Size and its new Size.

Size Cost Cramped 500 gold Roomy 1,000 gold Vast 3,000 gold

docs.title: Special Facilities
docs.text:
A Special Facility is a location that helps characters work on specific tasks that help them while adventuring. Each Bastion starts with 2 Special Facilities.

Facility Prerequisite Description Arcanum Spellcasting with an Arcane Focus Craft and study arcane magic and its items. Armory — Stock weapons and armor to equip your allies. Garden Spellcasting with a Druidic Focus Cultivate useful plants, herbs, and produce. Infirmary — Tend the wounded and recover from injury. Kitchen — Prepare meals that fortify your allies. Shrine Spellcasting with a Holy Symbol A holy site for blessings and divine aid. Storehouse — Stockpile trade goods to buy and sell. Studio Spellcasting with a Musical Instrument Description TBD Study — A quiet place for research and scribing. Training Yard Fighting Style Drill recruits and hone martial skill. Workshop — Craft mundane gear and clever inventions.

docs.title: Hirelings
docs.text: Every Special Facility comes with at least one Hireling who works in and maintains it. A facility's Hireling is proficient with any Tools or Skills tied to that Facility and can help with checks or crafting.

docs.title: Adding Special Facilities
docs.text:
Unlike Basic Facilities, Special Facilities can't be bought; you gain more at specific Character Levels.

Character Level Special Facilities 5 2 9 3 13 4 17 5

docs.title: Changing Special Facilities
docs.text: When you gain a Level, you can change one of your Special Facilities.

docs.title: Upgrading Special Facilities
docs.text:
Upgrading a Special Facility increases its Size and costs the difference between its current Size and its new Size. Each facility also gives additional effects as its size increases.

Size Cost Cramped — Roomy 2,000 gold Vast 7,000 gold

docs.title: Traits
docs.text: Traits are the measurable facts that define a creature on a stat block or character sheet.

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
Six Abilities measure a creature's raw physical and mental capabilities. Each Ability is a number from -5 to +10 you add to the rolls and traits it governs.

Ability Description Uses Strength Physical might Melee Attacks, Heavy Armor, Damage Reduction, Jump Distance Dexterity Accuracy, agility, and balance Ranged Attacks, Light Armor, Initiative, Reflex Saves Constitution Health and stamina Hit Points, Fortitude Saves, Concentration Intelligence Reasoning, learning, and memory Spellcasting, Studying, additional Proficiencies Wisdom Awareness, empathy, and mental resilience Spellcasting, Will Saves, Searching Charisma Confidence, poise, and charm Spellcasting, Socializing

docs.title: Creature Type
docs.text: A Creature Type is a broad family a creature belongs to. Every creature has at least one Creature Type, and some have two. Most Creature Types share common traits, and some features and Spells single out specific types.

docs.title: Planar Creatures
docs.text:
A Planar creature is an Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, or Undead. Planar creatures have links to specific planes, which can be exploited by certain effects.

Creature Type Plane Aberration The Far Realms Celestial An Upper Plane Elemental An Inner Plane Fey The Feywild Fiend A Lower Plane Undead The Shadowfell

docs.title: Alignment
docs.text:
Alignment is a creature's moral and ethical outlook, summarized across two dimensions: a creature's regard for others, and its respect for order.

Lawful Neutral Chaotic Good Do the right thing as expected by society. Do the best they can, working within rules but not feeling bound by them. Act as conscience directs, with little regard for what others expect. Neutral Act in accordance with law, tradition, or a personal code, unswayed by the needs of others or the temptations of evil. Avoid moral questions and don't take sides, doing what seems best at the time. Follow their whims, valuing personal freedom above all else. Evil Methodically take what they want within the limits of a code of tradition, loyalty, or order. Do whatever they can get away with, untroubled by the harm they cause. Act with arbitrary violence, spurred by hatred or bloodlust.

docs.title: Reach
docs.text: A creature's Reach is how far it can manipulate objects and use any item, weapon, attack, or Spell that requires direct contact.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: Languages are the tongues a creature can speak, read, and understand.

docs.title: Standard Languages
docs.text:
Standard Languages are widespread on the Material Plane.

Language Typical Speakers Common anyone Common Sign Language anyone Dwarvish Dwarves Elvish Elves Giant Giants Gnomish Gnomes Goblin goblinoids Halfling Halflings Orcish Orcs

docs.title: Exotic Languages
docs.text:
Exotic Languages are less common on the Material Plane but more common on the Outer Planes.

Language Typical Speakers Abyssal demons Celestial Celestials Deep Speech Aberrations Draconic Dragons Druidic Druids Infernal devils Primordial Elementals Sylvan Fey Thieves' Cant Rogues Undercommon Underdark citizens

docs.title: Primordial Dialects
docs.text:
Primordial is spoken in four dialects, one for each of the primary elements.

Dialect Typical Speakers Aquan creatures of water Auran creatures of air Ignan creatures of fire Terran creatures of earth

The dialects share a common root, and a speaker of any one of them understands the other three. Which dialect a creature speaks says nothing about who it can talk to, but a great deal about where it came from.

docs.title: Other Languages
docs.text: Other Languages exist, but knowledge of them is rare outside their native speakers. Your background or experiences during an adventure may let you learn them.

docs.title: Telepathy
docs.text: Telepathy allows creatures to communicate mentally within a specified range. Unless a feature says otherwise, telepathic communication doesn't require a shared language, though both creatures must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic to understand.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Features are the special techniques and effects a creature uses to interact with the world and defend themselves in combat.

docs.title: Recharge
docs.text:
A Recharge feature lists a die result alongside its cost. Using the effect expends it, and it can't be used again until it recharges.

After the user's Turn ends while the effect is expended, they roll 1d6. On a result within the listed range, the effect recharges and can be used again. It also recharges after a Short Rest.

Rolling at the end of a Turn means a recharged effect is available for the whole of the next Round, so everyone can see it coming and has time to respond.

docs.title: Non-Player Characters
docs.text: Non-Player Characters are the other creatures a party meets in the world.

docs.title: Disposition
docs.text:
A creature's Disposition describes its attitude toward a Party; a group of Allies with collective relationships with other creatures. A creature holds a single Disposition toward a party, and every member of that party shares it.

Relationships are shaped by a wide array of roleplaying factors, but sort into three Dispositions:

Disposition Behavior Ally Fights with or for the party, and will put itself at risk for their sake. Independent No desire to help or harm the party. Most creatures are Independent by default. Enemy Actively antagonistic. Combat begins when an Enemy becomes aware of the party.

Disposition indicates how a creature is likely to behave, not its role in the story. Most creatures, including antagonists, are Independent until they are moved to aid a party or to do battle against it.

An Ally may still disagree with the party, and an Enemy might be talked into negotiating, depending on the situation and its motivations. A creature's Disposition can change over the course of play; the exact process is a roleplay decision the DM adjudicates, though some Spells and features can influence it.

docs.title: Companions
docs.text: Some Spells and features grant Companions, conjured Allies you share a magical link with, that travel with you and aid you in combat and exploration.

docs.title: Commanding Companions
docs.text:
Your Companions share your Turn in Initiative, but have their own Actions and movement.

The feature or Spell that gives you a Companion also describes how to command it to move and act (no matter how many commands you issue, a companion still has the normal action budget for a creature). If you don't command a Companion, it Dodges and moves to stay within 10 feet of you, avoiding danger if it can.

While you are Incapacitated, your Companions can act and Move on their own (no longer limited to dodging).

docs.title: Companion Proficiency
docs.text: Your Companions use your Character Level and Proficiency Bonus.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
Your Companions understand every language you speak, and may also know languages of its own.

You gain 120 feet of Telepathy with your Companions.

docs.title: Familiars
docs.text: A Familiar is a special Companion, such as the one created by Find Familiar. You can usually have only one Familiar at a time.

docs.title: Dismiss / Recall
docs.text:
Magic Action

You can temporarily dismiss your Familiar to a pocket dimension. Using this action again teleports your Familiar to within 30 feet of you.

docs.title: Sharing Senses
docs.text: While your Familiar is within 120 feet of you, you can see and hear through its senses; while doing so, you are Blinded and Deafened to your own senses.

docs.title: Switch Senses
docs.text:
Free Action

You can switch between your own senses and your Familiar's.

docs.title: Deliver Spell
docs.text: Before you cast a Reach Spell, your Familiar can use its Reaction to deliver the Spell through its Reach instead.

docs.title: Mounts
docs.text: You can Mount any Ally that has suitable anatomy and is at least 1 Size larger than you.

docs.title: Commanding a Mount
docs.text:
While mounted, your mount shares your Turn in Initiative, but has its own Actions and movement.

You can command your mount or let it act on its own (no matter how many commands you issue, a mount still has the normal action budget for a creature). An uncommanded mount moves and acts as it wishes, and has no restrictions on its Action.

An intelligent mount decides whether it allows itself to be commanded, and may refuse commands it disagrees with.

docs.title: Command
docs.text:
Free Action

You can command your mount to move and Dash, Disengage, or Dodge.

docs.title: Mount / Dismount
docs.text: You can spend half your movement (minimum 5 feet) to mount or dismount a creature within Reach.

docs.title: Staying Mounted
docs.text:
There are three different ways for you to become dismounted.

Dismount You are Propelled After an effect propels you while you are mounted, you are dismounted. Your Mount is Propelled/You are Knocked Prone If an effect propels your mount, or you are knocked Prone while mounted, you make a Reflex Save (DC 10).Fail. You are dismounted and land Prone within 5 feet of your mount.Success. You stay mounted and don't fall Prone. Your Mount is Knocked Prone Before your mount is knocked Prone, you can use your Reaction to dismount safely. Otherwise, you are dismounted and land Prone within 5 feet of your mount.

docs.title: Swarms
docs.text:
A Swarm is a group of many Tiny or Small creatures treated as a single creature, and it uses its member's stat block with the following changes:

  • Its Size is Medium, or Large if its members fly.
  • Its Strength increases by 2.
  • Its Hit Die increases one step (along d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20).
  • Its Level is set by the effect that produces it, and its Hit Dice, Hit Points, Armor Class, and Attack Roll follow from that Level as normal.
  • It makes a single attack that deals its member's damage dice for each Level of the Swarm, to a minimum of 1d4 per Level (the attack's Ability is only added once).
  • It deals half damage while Bloodied.
  • It can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for one of its members.
  • It can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.
  • It gains Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing Resistance.
  • It gains Charm, Fear, Grapple, Paralysis, Petrification, Prone, Restraint, and Stun Immunity.

docs.text: Owlbears have the body of a bear and the head and temper of a great owl, and no one agrees on where the first one came from. They are relentlessly territorial and attack anything that crosses into their range.

docs.title: Wight
docs.text: Wights are the corpses of warriors and rulers kept upright by a hunger for the living. They retain the cunning and gear they carried in life, and those they drain rise as zombies to serve them.

docs.title: Wight
docs.text:
Medium Undead, Neutral Evil

Speed 30 ft. Reach 5 ft. Skills Perception, Stealth Level 6 Proficiency Bonus +3 Features Sunlight Sensitivity While in Sunlight, the wight gains Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls. Multiattack The wight makes 2 attacks, using Necrotic Sword or Necrotic Bow in any combination. It can replace one attack with Life Drain.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Necrotic Sword Melee Attack Range Reach Attack +5 to hit [STR + PB] Damage 1d10 + 2 Slashing Damage [1d10 + STR] and 1d8 Necrotic Damage Necrotic Bow Ranged Attack Range 150/600 ft. Attack +5 to hit [DEX + PB] Damage 1d10 + 2 Piercing Damage [1d10 + DEX] and 1d8 Necrotic Damage Life Drain Normal Action One creature within 5 feet makes a Fortitude Save (DC 14 [8 + CON + PB]); on a failure, the wight deals 1d8 + 2 Necrotic Damage [1d8 + STR] and the target's Hit Point Maximum decreases by that amount.  A Humanoid slain by this effect rises 24 hours later as a Zombie under the wight's control, unless it is restored to life or its body is destroyed.  The wight can control up to 12 Zombies at a time.

docs.title: Elephant
docs.text: Elephants are herd animals of the savanna and jungle, placid until threatened and devastating when they aren't. A charging elephant goes through most obstacles rather than around them.

docs.title: Air Elemental
docs.text: Air Elementals are living winds, visible only as a churning column of dust and debris. They move faster than anything on the ground and can pass through a crack no wider than a finger.

docs.text: Bulettes tunnel through solid earth and surface underneath their prey, and they hunt by the tremors of footsteps overhead. They eat almost anything that walks and are called landsharks for good reason.

docs.title: Aberration Bestiary
docs.text: Aberrations are alien creatures from beyond the physical realms, warped in body and mind. Their forms defy anatomy, their motives defy understanding, and few who meet one come away unchanged.

docs.title: Beast Bestiary
docs.text: Beasts are the natural animals of the world. They act on instinct rather than reason, and are commonly hunted, tamed, or ridden.

docs.title: Celestial Bestiary
docs.text: Celestials are natives of the Upper Planes, embodiments of virtue and light. Many serve the gods as messengers and warriors, and even the least of them burns bright against the dark.

docs.title: Construct Bestiary
docs.text: Constructs are objects given animation and a purpose. They typically follow the will of their makers rather than any of their own.

docs.title: Dragon Bestiary
docs.text: Dragons are ancient creatures of immense power and pride. The oldest command devastating magic and hoard what they covet, and their cunning grows with every century.

docs.title: Elemental Bestiary
docs.text: Elementals are beings of raw elemental matter — fire, water, earth, air, and any combination thereof. They hail from the Elemental Planes, and rarely think or feel as mortals do.

docs.title: Fey Bestiary
docs.text: Fey are creatures of the Feywild, bound to the wild magic of nature. Whimsical and capricious, they blur the line between beauty and menace, and their bargains rarely mean what they seem.

docs.title: Fiend Bestiary
docs.text: Fiends are natives of the Lower Planes, born of corruption and ruin. Devils bargain for souls while demons crave only destruction, and both treat mortals as playthings in their designs.

docs.title: Giant Bestiary
docs.text: Giants are towering humanoids that dwarf the common folk, heirs to an ancient and ordered world. Giants are long-lived, few in number, and boast tremendous might and long memories.

docs.title: Humanoid Bestiary
docs.text: Humanoids are the peoples of the world, from Primes and Elves to Orcs and Goblinoids, and every other folk who inhabit it. They raise the civilizations most adventurers call home, and stand among their most common allies and foes.

docs.title: Monstrosity Bestiary
docs.text: Monstrosities are frightening creatures born of magic or mythology, uncanny yet nonetheless part of the natural world. Few can be reasoned with, and fewer still tamed.

docs.title: Ooze Bestiary
docs.text: Oozes are amorphous masses that slither, seep, and engulf. Most lack true minds, driven by nothing but the urge to consume whatever they touch.

docs.title: Plant Bestiary
docs.text: Plants are vegetal creatures and fungal growths given strange life. Some root in place and wait, while others walk, hunt, and hunger like any predator.

docs.title: Undead Bestiary
docs.text: Undead are once-living creatures returned by necromancy or a will too restless for the grave. They shamble, hunger, and crave the living they can no longer join.

docs.title: Character Creation
docs.text: Character Sheets v1 with Spell Sheet

docs.title: 1. Choose Abilities
docs.text: Your Abilities start at 0, the baseline for a typical person. When you create your character, choose 4 Abilities to increase by 1 each.

docs.title: 2. Choose a Race
docs.text:
Your Race outlines your physical characteristics and grants you a set of Traits and Features. Each race includes:

  • 2 Abilities, which each increase by 1
  • a Creature Type
  • a Size
  • a Speed
  • a Reach
  • starting Hit Points
  • Resistances, Protections, or Immunities (if any)
  • Senses (if any)
  • at least 1 Feature

docs.title: 3. Choose a Background
docs.text:
Your Background represents the place and occupation that was most formative before you became an adventurer.

You can create your own background, or you can modify one of the Example Backgrounds to suit your character. Each background includes:

  • 3 Abilities, which each increase by 1
  • 1 Origin Feat
  • 2 Skill Proficiencies
  • 1 Skill Expertise
  • 1 Trade Proficiency
  • 3 Languages: Common, 1 Standard, and 1 Exotic
  • 1 Common Magic Item
  • 50 gold

docs.title: 4. Choose a Class
docs.text:
Your Class reflects your specialized training and defines how you interact with the world. The class you choose at level 1 is your Primary Class, which includes the following parts:

  • 1 Starting Ability, which increases by 1
  • a Hit Die
  • a set of Starting Equipment
  • 1 Saving Throw Proficiency
  • 1 Saving Throw Aptitude
  • Weapon and Armor Proficiencies
  • Skill Proficiencies
  • Trade Proficiencies
  • Level 1 Class Features

docs.title: 5. Purchase Equipment
docs.text: Your class and background include starting items and gold. You can purchase additional items for their listed value.

docs.title: 6. Finishing Touches
docs.text: After choosing your abilities, proficiencies, and equipment, it’s time to calculate your bonuses and finish your character sheet.

docs.title: Hit Point Maximum
docs.text: Add your Race’s starting Hit Points, the maximum of your Primary Class’s Hit Die, and your Constitution. This total is your Hit Point Maximum.

docs.title: Armor Class
docs.text: Calculate your Armor Class based on the Armor you wear, if any.

docs.title: Intelligence Proficiencies
docs.text:
Creatures learn additional Proficiencies and Languages based on their Intelligence. If your Intelligence decreases, you don't lose any learned Proficiencies, but you don't learn more until your Intelligence exceeds the highest Intelligence you've gained a Proficiency from.

If you would gain Proficiency in a Skill, you can instead gain Proficiency with a Trade or learn a Language.

If you would gain Expertise, you can instead gain Proficiency in a Skill, Proficiency with a Trade, or learn a Language.

Intelligence You Learn 0- — 1 Proficiency with a Trade, or a Language 2 Proficiency in a Skill 3 Proficiency with a Trade, or a Language 4 Expertise in a Skill you're Proficient in 5 Proficiency with a Trade, or a Language 6 Proficiency in a Skill 7 Expertise in a Skill you're Proficient in 8 Proficiency in a Skill 9 Proficiency in a Skill 10+ Expertise in a Skill you're Proficient in

docs.title: Proficiency Bonuses
docs.text: Calculate your bonuses to Skills, Saving Throws, and Attacks. Find the relevant Ability for that bonus and add your Proficiency Bonus based on your level of Proficiency.

docs.title: Saving Throw DCs
docs.text: Calculate your Saving Throw DCs for features, such as Spellcasting. Find the relevant Ability for that feature, add your Proficiency Bonus, and add 8.

docs.title: Starting at Higher Levels
docs.text:
To create a character at a higher level, start by creating them at Level 1 and Level Up one at a time.

You also gain additional gold and Magic Items based on your starting Level:

docs.title: Class Levels
docs.text: Your Level in a class represents the depth of your training. Each of your classes' levels are tracked individually.

docs.title: Leveling Up
docs.text:
When you gain a Level, choose 1 of your classes to gain that Level in (if you don't have a Secondary Class yet, you can choose 1). You gain:

  • the chosen class’s Features for that Level
  • one of the chosen class's Hit Die

docs.title: Character Level
docs.text:
Your Character Level is the sum of your Levels in all your classes. Your Character Level determines your Proficiency Bonus, your Ability Maximum, and gives additional Feats and/or bonuses to an Ability.

docs.title: Primary Class
docs.text:
Your Primary Class is the class you choose at Level 1. When you gain your first Level in your Primary Class:

  • you gain that class's Starting Equipment and Primary Proficiencies
  • your class's Starting Ability increases by 1

docs.title: Secondary Class
docs.text:
Your Secondary Class is the second class you choose at a later Level. Once you choose a Secondary Class, you cannot change it, and you cannot take Levels in a third class. When you gain your first Level in your Secondary Class, you gain that class’s Secondary Proficiencies.

If you gain the Spellcasting feature from both your Classes, your total total Spell Slots depends on each Classes' individual capacity for magic.

docs.title: Starting Ability
docs.text: Each Class has a Starting Ability, the Ability improved when you take that Class at Level 1. If a Class offers a choice of Starting Ability, you choose 1 when you gain your first Level in it.

docs.title: Class Ability
docs.text: Most Classes also have a Class Ability, the Ability that determines the effectiveness of their features. A Class's Class Ability is often the same as its Starting Ability, some Classes use a different one, and a few have no Class Ability of their own; instead, their Subclasses may grant one.

docs.text: Artificers are inventors who channel magic through tools, devices, and infused creations, turning craftsmanship into power.

docs.title: 1: Infuse Items

After a Long Rest, you can infuse Magic Item effects into appropriate nearby items, creating temporary items as needed. Temporary items have no Value and vanish once their Infusions end.

You can Attune to an item you infuse immediately.

The Artificer Table shows how many items you can infuse. To infuse more items, choose existing Infusions to end first.

docs.text: The range of your Telepathy and sense sharing with your assistant extends to 5 miles while on the same plane. Additionally, you are not Blinded or Deafened while perceiving through your assistant's senses.

docs.title: Improved Spell Delivery
docs.text: Your assistant can deliver any Spell, not just Reach Spells (A Spell that targets Self targets the assistant instead of you).

docs.title: 3: Adventurer's Atlas
docs.text:
After a Long Rest, you can conjure an Adventurer's Atlas. The atlas disappears if you conjure another Adventurer's Atlas.

The atlas contains your name and up to Class Ability additional names (minimum 1). A creature can only write its own name in the atlas, and you can erase any other name in the atlas by touching it. (You can remove your name from the atlas, though that doesn't allow you to add another creature in your place.)

docs.title: Global Positioning
docs.text: Creatures in the atlas always know the general location and direction to other creatures in the atlas, and don't need to see to target each other with magical effects.

docs.title: Terrain Advantage
docs.text: The Initiative Checks of creatures in the atlas increase by 1d4.

docs.title: Secret Shortcuts
docs.text: Free Action; 15 feet of movement: You can teleport up to 10 feet.

docs.title: 6: Ingenious Movement
docs.text:
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.

Before or after you expend a use of Improvise, one creature in your Adventurer's Atlas can teleport up to 30 feet.

docs.title: Perfect Pathfinding
docs.text: You learn Find the Path.

docs.title: Free Casting
docs.text: Once per Long Rest: You can cast Find the Path without a Spell Slot or Components.

docs.title: Safe Haven
docs.text:
Free Action: Before a creature in your Adventurer's Atlas would drop to 0 Hit Points or be killed, you can remove its name from the atlas to set its Hit Points to LV × 2 instead, then teleport it to within 5 feet of another creature in the atlas.

A creature whose name you remove this way can't write its name in the atlas again until you finish a Long Rest.

docs.text:
After a Short Rest, you regain 1 use of Rage.

After a Long Rest, you regain all uses of Rage.

docs.title: Enrage
docs.text:
Bonus Action; 1 Rage use: You can move up to half your Speed. Then, you gain the following effects until the end of your next Turn:

  • You gain Physical Resistance, Fortitude Protection, and Advantage on Strength Checks.
  • Your Strength Attacks add your Rage Bonus to Damage. The Barbarian Table shows your Rage Bonus.
  • You can use Strength to make Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival Checks.
  • You can't cast Spells or Concentrate.

Your Rage ends early if you become Incapacitated or don Heavy Armor.

docs.title: Extending Rage
docs.text:
You can extend your Rage's duration to the end of your next Turn, up to a maximum of 10 minutes, by doing 1 of the following:

  • Attack an Enemy.
  • Cause an Enemy to make a Saving Throw.
  • Use a Bonus Action to extend your Rage (no Rage uses required).

Free Action; Once per Turn: Before you Attack with Advantage, you can lose Advantage on the Attack Roll. If you do, you add 1d10 to the Damage and choose 1 of the following effects:

Effect Forceful Blow After the Attack, you propel the target up to 15 feet away from you, then propel yourself up to half your Speed toward the target. Hamstring Blow After the Attack, you decrease the target's Speed by 15 feet until the start of your next Turn.

docs.text:

Sundering Blow After the Attack, you add 5 to the next Attack Roll another creature makes against the target before the start of your next Turn.

docs.title: 8: Relentless Rage
docs.text:
Free Action: Before you drop to 0 Hit Points while Raging, you can make a Fortitude Save (DC 10).

Fail No effect. Success Your Hit Points become 2 × Character Level.

Then, the DC for this Saving Throw increases by 5.

After a Short Rest, the DC for this Saving Throw resets to 10.

docs.text: Your Rage lasts for 10 minutes and doesn't end early unless you choose to end it, become Unconscious (not Incapacitated), or don Heavy Armor.

docs.title: Unending Rage
docs.text: Free Action; Once per Long Rest: You can regain all expended uses of Rage.

docs.text: Your Strength and Constitution (and your maximum for those Abilities) increase by 2.

docs.title: Path of the Wild Heart Barbarian
docs.text:
Barbarians who follow the Path of the Wild Heart see themselves as kin to the beasts of the world. They learn to speak with animals, and their Rage takes on the aspect of a wild creature, filling them with ever-shifting primal might.

docs.title: College of Eloquence Bard
docs.text:
Bards of the College of Eloquence master the art of oratory, wielding a well-reasoned argument as deftly as any blade. They blend logic and theatrical wordplay to win over skeptics and stir the hearts of any audience.

docs.text: If a creature adds your Inspiration Die to an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw and still fails, that creature doesn't spend the Inspiration Die.

docs.text: Reaction; Class Ability times (minimum 1) per Long Rest: After a creature within 60 feet adds your Inspiration Die to an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw and succeeds, you can give a second creature within 60 feet an Inspiration Die (without expending a use of Bardic Inspiration).

docs.title: College of Lore Bard
docs.text:
Bards of the College of Lore gather knowledge from every source, from scholarly tomes to peasant tales. They hold audiences spellbound, then leave them questioning all they once held true, loyal to nothing but beauty and truth.

docs.title: 3: War Pact
docs.text:
You can bond a Weapon into a Pact Weapon. You can only have up to 2 Pact Weapons at a time, and you can't bond with a Weapon that is Attuned or bonded to another creature.

You can use your Pact Weapons as an Arcane Focus, and while not Incapacitated, you can't be disarmed of your Pact Weapons.

docs.title: Bond Weapon
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can turn a Weapon within your Reach into a Pact Weapon.

docs.title: Recall Weapon

docs.title: War Casting
docs.text: 2 Attack Actions: You can cast a 2nd-Level or lower Spell with a Casting Time under 1 minute.

docs.title: Monk
docs.text: Monks are martial artists who channel a wellspring of inner energy, striking with speed and precision beyond their physical limitations.

docs.title: 1: Ki
docs.text:
You gain LV Ki. You can spend Ki to use Monk Features.

If a Ki effect requires a Saving Throw, its DC is 8 + Class Ability + PB.

docs.title: Regaining Ki
docs.text: After a Short Rest, you regain all uses of Ki.

docs.title: Quick Focus
docs.text: Free Action; Once per Long Rest: Before you roll Initiative, you can regain all uses of Ki.

docs.title: 1: Unarmored Stance
docs.text: While you are Unarmored and don't have a Shield donned, you gain the following effects:

docs.title: Unarmored Defense
docs.text: Your base Armor Class becomes 8 + DEX + Class Ability + PB.

docs.title: Unarmored Movement
docs.text: Your Speed increases, and you can move along vertical surfaces and across liquids without falling during your movement. The Monk Table shows your bonus Speed, and when this bonus increases.

docs.title: Unarmored Fall
docs.text: Reaction: Before you take Falling Damage, you can reduce that damage by LV × 5.

docs.title: 1: Martial Arts
docs.text: You learn the Striker Fighting Style and can use it with Monk Weapons (in addition to Unarmed Strikes). The Damage Die increases as you gain Monk Levels, as shown in the Monk Table.

docs.title: Monk Weapons
docs.text: Unarmed Strikes, Simple Melee Weapons, and Light Martial Melee Weapons are Monk Weapons. You can use some Monk Features only with these Weapons, and some Monk Subclasses expand which Weapons are Monk Weapons.

docs.title: Flurry of Blows
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can make 1 Unarmed Strike. Then, you can expend 1 Ki to make an additional Unarmed Strike.

docs.title: Patient Defense
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can Disengage. Then, you can expend 1 Ki to Dodge.

docs.title: Step of the Wind
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can Dash. Then, you can expend 1 Ki to Disengage, and your jump distance doubles until the end of your Turn.

docs.title: 2: Deflecting Palm
docs.text: Reaction: Before you take Physical Damage from an Attack, you can reduce that damage by 1d10 + DEX + LV.

docs.title: Redirect
docs.text:
Free Action; 1 Ki use: After this feature reduces an Attack's damage to 0, you can redirect the Attack. If the Attack was a Melee Attack, choose 1 creature within Reach. If the Attack was a Ranged Attack, choose 1 creature within 60 feet. The target makes a Reflex Save.

Fail You deal 2 Martial Arts Dice + DEX damage of the original Attack's type. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: 2: Fighting Style
docs.text: You learn Fighting Styles. The Monk Table shows how many Fighting Styles you know.

docs.title: Changing Fighting Styles
docs.text: Whenever you level up, you can change one of your Fighting Styles.

docs.title: 3: Monk Subclass
docs.text:
Choose a Monk Subclass.

Your subclass grants you a feature at this level.

Subclasses

docs.title: 4: Stunning Strike
docs.text:
Free Action; 1 Ki use: After you hit with a Monk Weapon, you can force the target to make a Fortitude Save.

Fail You stun the target until the end of your next Turn. Success The target's Speed halves until the end of your next Turn.

docs.title: 5: Extra Attack
docs.text: The number of Attacks you can make with your Attack Action increases by 1.

docs.title: 6: Subclass Feature
docs.text: Your subclass grants you an additional feature.

docs.title: 7: Evasion
docs.text: You gain Reflex Evasion.

docs.title: 8: Self-Restoration
docs.text: You gain Starvation and Dehydration Immunity.

docs.title: Rebalance
docs.text: Free Action: After your Turn ends, you can end 1 Charm, Fear, or Sickness on yourself (these conditions can't prevent using this feature).

docs.title: 9: Subclass Feature
docs.text: Your subclass grants you an additional feature.

docs.title: Unending Ki
docs.text: Before you roll Initiative, if you have 3 or fewer Ki, you regain expended Ki until you have 4.

docs.title: Perfect Form
docs.text:
Spending Ki on your Martial Arts grants the following effects:

Feature Flurry of Blows The number of Unarmed Strikes you can make increases by 1. Patient Defense Free Action: You can gain 2 Martial Arts Dice Temporary Hit Points. Step of the Wind Free Action: Whenever you move on the same Turn, you can propel one Ally within Reach with you.

docs.title: Enlightened
docs.text: You gain Proficiency in all Saving Throws.

docs.title: Inevitable
docs.text: Free Action; 1 Ki use: Before you fail a Saving Throw, you can reroll it. The second time you use this feature on the same Saving Throw, you succeed instead.

docs.title: 6: Subclass Feature

docs.title: 9: Subclass Feature
docs.text: Your subclass grants you an additional feature.

docs.title: 10: Improved Divine Aura
docs.text: Your Divine Aura increases to 30 feet.

docs.title: 11: Avatar of Conviction

docs.title: Oath of Glory Paladin
docs.text:
Glory Paladins believe they and their companions are destined to achieve glory through great deeds of heroism. They train diligently and encourage their companions, so they're all ready when destiny calls.

Level Features 3 Glory Spells,Peerless Athlete,Inspiring Smite 6 Aura of Alacrity 9 Glorious Defense 11 Avatar of Legends

docs.title: Tenets
docs.text:
The Oath of Glory teaches the following tenets:

  • Endeavor to be known by your deeds.
  • Face hardships with courage.
  • Inspire others to strive for glory.

docs.title: 3: Glory Spells
docs.text:
You learn the following Spells at the corresponding Paladin Levels.

Level Spells 3rd Guiding Bolt, Heroism 5th Enhance Ability, Magic Weapon 9th Haste, Protection from Energy

docs.title: 3: Channel Conviction: Peerless Athlete
docs.text: Bonus Action; 1 Channel Conviction use: You gain the following effects for 10 minutes: - You gain Advantage on Athletics and Acrobatics Checks. - Your maximum Long Jump and High Jump distances increase by 10 feet.

docs.title: 3: Channel Conviction: Inspiring Smite
docs.text:
Bonus Action; 1 Channel Conviction use: After you cast Divine Smite, you can give 2d8 + LV Temporary Hit Points, divided among any creatures within 30 feet.

Add 1d8 to the Temporary Hit Points at Character Level 5, 9, 13, and 17.

docs.title: 6: Aura of Alacrity
docs.text:
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.

After an Ally enters your Divine Aura for the first time on a turn (including when they start their turn there), you increase their Speed by 10 feet until the end of the Turn.

docs.title: 9: Glorious Defense
docs.text: Reaction; Class Ability times per Long Rest: Before you or an Ally within your Divine Aura is hit with an Attack, you can add Class Ability to the target's Armor Class. Then, if the Attack misses, you can attack the attacker.

docs.title: 11: Avatar of Legends
docs.text:
When you use your Avatar of Conviction, you gain the following effects:

  • You gain Advantage on Charisma Checks.
  • Once per Turn: Before you fail a Saving Throw, you can succeed instead.
  • Once per Turn: Before you miss an Attack Roll, you can hit instead.

docs.text: Rangers are hunters and trackers at home in the wilds, blending martial skill, primal magic, and knowledge of their quarry.

After a Long Rest, you regain all uses of Marked Target.

docs.title: Improved Mark
docs.text:
Your Hunter's Mark gains the following effects:

  • The additional damage increases as you gain Ranger Levels, as shown in the Ranger Table.
  • You can move the Mark regardless of the target's Hit Points.
  • You can cast this Spell (no Concentration required). If you do, the Spell's Duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

docs.text: The number of Attacks you can make with your Attack Action increases by 1.

docs.text: Your subclass grants you an additional feature.

docs.text: After a Short Rest, your Exhaustion decreases by 1.

docs.title: Additional Imprints

docs.title: 9: Subclass Feature
docs.text: Your subclass grants you an additional feature.

docs.title: 10: Imprinting Master
docs.text: You gain additional options for your Primal Imprint.

docs.title: Retarget
docs.text: Free Action: After your Turn starts, you can move your Hunter's Mark to a new creature within range.

docs.title: Exploit Weakness
docs.text: Free Action: Before you deal damage to a creature Marked by you, you can end your Hunter's Mark to give the target Vulnerability to that damage (If the damage was from an Attack, you still add the bonus damage before applying Vulnerability).

docs.title: Beast Master Ranger
docs.text:
Beast Masters fight alongside a Primal Companion, a loyal beast bonded to them as a partner in battle.

Level Features 3 Beast Master Spells,Primal Companion 6 Superior Training 9 Exceptional Training Primal Companion Forms Land Sea Sky

docs.title: 3: Beast Master Spells
docs.text:
Your specialization grants you additional Spells. You learn these Spells at the corresponding Ranger Levels.

Level Spells 3rd Cure Wounds 5th Warding Bond 9th Haste

docs.title: 3: Primal Companion
docs.text:
You conjure a Primal Companion.

Your companion's Ability Checks and Saving Throws increase by PB.

docs.title: Changing Companions
docs.text: After a Long Rest, you can change your companion's form to another Primal Companion.

docs.title: Primal Command
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can command your companion to move and take any Action available to it (including the Attack Action).

docs.title: Attack
docs.text: Attack Action: You can command your companion to move and Attack.

docs.title: Share Spell
docs.text: Free Action: Before you cast a Spell that targets only you, you can also target your companion if it is within 120 feet.

docs.title: Revive Companion
docs.text: 1 minute; 1 Marked Target use: If your companion is dead, you can revive it with all its Hit Points.

docs.title: Magical Strikes
docs.text: Your companion's Beast Strike can deal Force Damage instead of its normal Damage Type.

docs.title: Advanced Commands
docs.text: Your Primal Command can also direct your companion to use its Bonus Action to Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help.

docs.title: Apex Companion
docs.text: After you change your companion's form, you can increase its Size by 1.

docs.title: Bestial Fury
docs.text: The number of Attacks your companion can make with its Attack Action increases by 1.

docs.title: Strike Mastery
docs.text: Your companion's Beast Strike can use the Graze or Sap Weapon Technique.

docs.title: Primal Imprints
docs.text: Primal Imprints are the traits a Ranger has learned by studying beasts in the wild, adopting a creature's own gifts as their own.

docs.title: Bioluminescence
docs.text: Magic Action: You can emit Bright Light out to 10 feet and Dim Light 10 feet further until you use this Action again.

docs.title: Camouflage
docs.text: Other creatures gain Disadvantage on Perception Checks to see you.

docs.title: Hold Breath
docs.text: You can hold your breath for up to 1 hour.

docs.title: Keen Senses
docs.text: You gain Advantage on Perception Checks that rely on hearing or sight.

docs.title: Powerful Build
docs.text: You gain Advantage on Athletics Checks, and your Jump distance doubles.

docs.title: Sure-Footed
docs.text: You gain Prone Protection, and you gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

docs.title: Amphibious
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

You can breathe underwater, and you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

docs.title: Cold Tolerance
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

You gain Cold Resistance, you can tolerate temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower without additional protection, and you ignore Difficult Terrain created by ice or snow.

docs.title: Heat Tolerance
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

You gain Fire Resistance, you can tolerate temperatures of 100 degrees Fahrenheit or higher without additional protection, and you ignore Difficult Terrain created by sand.

docs.title: Jumper
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

You can use your Dexterity to determine your Jump distance, and you gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

docs.title: Mimicry
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

You can mimic simple sounds you have heard. A creature that hears the sounds can make an Insight Check against your Ranger Spell Save DC to identify them as imitations.

docs.title: Nocturnal
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

You gain 120 feet of Darkvision.

docs.title: Roving
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks, and your Speed increases by 10 feet.

docs.title: Skittish
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 4 Ranger

Bonus Action: You can Disengage or Hide.

docs.title: Amorphous
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 7 Ranger

You gain Grapple Protection, and you can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without expending extra movement (Items you are wearing or carrying don't gain this effect).

docs.title: Echolocation
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 7 Ranger

While you aren't Deafened, you gain 30 feet of Blindsight.

docs.title: Glider
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 7 Ranger

You gain Falling Resistance. While it is your Turn, you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed (You fall if you end your Turn airborne without another way to stay aloft).

docs.title: Web Walker
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 7 Ranger

You gain a Spider Climb Speed equal to your Speed and you ignore movement penalties caused by webs.

docs.title: Burrower
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 10 Ranger

You gain a 15-foot Burrow Speed that leaves tunnels behind.

docs.title: Pack Tactics
docs.text:
Prerequisite: Level 10 Ranger

You gain Advantage on Attack Rolls against creatures that are within Reach of a non-Incapacitated Ally.

docs.title: Metamagic
docs.text: Metamagic is the art of bending a Spell as it's cast, letting a Sorcerer reshape its range, timing, or effect on the fly.

docs.title: Careful Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: Choose up to Sorcerer Ability creatures. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on Saving Throws against the Spell and take no damage from it.

docs.title: Distant Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: The Spell's Range becomes doubled. If the Spell has a Range of Reach, its Range becomes 30 feet instead.

docs.title: Empowered Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: The first time you make a Damage Roll for the Spell, you can reroll up to Sorcerer Ability Damage Dice. You can use this Metamagic even if you've already used a different Metamagic on the Spell.

docs.title: Extended Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: The Spell's Duration becomes doubled, up to a maximum of 24 hours. You gain Advantage on Concentration Saves for the Spell.

docs.title: Heightened Spell
docs.text: 2 Sorcery Points: Choose 1 target of the Spell. That target gains Disadvantage on Saving Throws against the Spell.

docs.title: Quickened Spell
docs.text: 2 Sorcery Points: If the Spell has a Casting Time of an Action, its Casting Time becomes a Bonus Action.

docs.title: Seeking Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: The first time you miss with an Attack Roll for the Spell, you can reroll the Attack Roll. You can use this Metamagic even if you've already used a different Metamagic on the Spell.

docs.title: Subtle Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: The Spell has no Components, except Material Components that are consumed or have a gold value.

docs.title: Transmuted Spell
docs.text: 1 Sorcery Point: You replace every instance of one Elemental Damage Type in the Spell with a different Elemental Damage Type.

docs.title: Twinned Spell
docs.text: Spell Level in Sorcery Points (minimum 1): If the Spell has exactly one target, you choose a second target.

docs.title: Eldritch Invocations
docs.text: Eldritch Invocations are lasting gifts drawn from a Warlock's patron, each a permanent enhancement to their magic and abilities.

docs.title: Armor of Shadows
docs.text: You learn Mage Armor and can cast it on yourself without a Spell Slot.

docs.title: Eldritch Mind
docs.text: You gain Concentration Protection.

docs.title: Lessons of the First Ones
docs.text:
Choose an Origin Feat or Initiate Fighting Style.

You learn that Feat.

docs.title: Repeatable
docs.text: You can learn this Invocation more than once, choosing a different feat each time.

docs.title: Pact of the Blade
docs.text:
You can conjure or bond a Pact Weapon. The bond ends if you bond another Weapon, your Pact Weapon leaves your Reach for 1 minute or more, or you die. While bonded, your Pact Weapon gains the following effects:

  • You can use it as an Arcane Focus.
  • You gain Proficiency with it.
  • Your Attacks with it can use your Warlock Ability.
  • It can deal Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant Damage instead of its normal Damage Type.

docs.title: Conjure Pact Weapon
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can conjure a Simple or Martial Melee Weapon to your hand and bond it as your Pact Weapon; it disappears after the bond ends.

docs.title: Bond Magic Weapon
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can bond a Magic Weapon you're carrying as your Pact Weapon. You can't bond a Weapon attuned or bonded to another creature.

docs.title: Pact of the Chain
docs.text: You learn Find Familiar and can cast it as a Magic Action without a Spell Slot. After you cast it, you can choose 1 of the following special forms for your Familiar: Imp, Quasit, Slaad Tadpole, or Sprite.

docs.title: Pact of the Tome
docs.text:
After a Short Rest, you can conjure a Book of Shadows to your hand. The book disappears if you conjure another or you die. You can use the book as an Arcane Focus.

After you conjure the book, choose 3 Cantrips and 2 1st-Level Ritual Spells. While the book is on your person, you know the chosen Spells as Warlock Spells.

docs.title: Agonizing Blast

Free Action; 1 Spell Slot: Before you damage a creature with your Pact Weapon, you can add 1d8 Force Damage, plus 1d8 for each Level of the Spell Slot expended. After you deal that damage, if the target is no more than 2 Sizes larger than you, you can knock it Prone.

docs.title: Feats
docs.text:
Feats are the special talents a character picks up along their adventures.

Feats Origin Feats Origin Feats are foundational talents a character learns at Level 1. General Feats General Feats are broadly useful talents a character earns as they level up. Fighting Styles Fighting Styles are martial combat specialties a character can learn. Ancestry Feats Ancestry Feats deepen a character's racial characteristics. Epic Boons Epic Boons are the legendary talents beyond mortal limits. Dragonmarks Dragonmarks are magical sigils passed down through bloodlines.

After you finish a Short Rest, you can don a suit of Armor you have Proficiency with. Until you doff the Armor, it gains the following effects:

  • Features and Spells treat you as though you were Unarmored.
  • You ignore the Armor's Stealth penalties.
  • Your Armor Class and Damage Reduction each increase by 1.
  • It takes 1 hour to doff the Armor.

Fail The target's Speed becomes halved until the start of its next Turn. Success No effect.

docs.title: Dragonmarks
docs.text: Dragonmarks are magical sigils passed down through bloodlines.

docs.title: Gaining Dragonmarks
docs.text: Possessing a Dragonmark requires a connection to the Mark's Sovereign — either by bloodline, or by acquaintance. As a result, taking a Dragonmark requires that the setting and story allow it. Your DM determines whether Dragonmarks are available, and can help weave the Mark's Sovereign into your character's backstory.

docs.title: Types of Dragonmarks
docs.text:
The most powerful Dragonmarks are passed down through a creature's family. Each Dragonmark has four forms:

Dragonmark Description Noble Mark A naturally manifested Dragonmark. Noble Marks can develop into Greater Marks of their own accord. Lesser Mark A Dragonmark granted by a house leader. Possesses the same might as a Noble Mark, but cannot develop further without the Sovereign's intervention. Greater Mark The height of a Dragonmark's power, each manifesting unique abilities that set their wielders apart from typical magic users. Sovereign Mark The singular leader of a Dragonmarked family. Sovereign Marks are able to grant Lesser and Greater Marks to other creatures.

docs.title: Greater Dragonmarks
docs.text: A Noble or Lesser Dragonmark's power can increase to a Greater Mark during a campaign. A Noble Mark usually develops when its wielder accomplishes a great feat, while a Lesser Mark requires the acknowledgement of the Mark's Sovereign. In either case, a Greater Mark usually isn't available earlier than Level 5.

docs.title: Aberrant Dragonmarks
docs.text: Dragonmarks almost always manifest their magic predictably and constructively. Aberrant Marks, however, manifest spontaneously often have unpredictable and dangerous powers.

docs.text: A Greater Mark builds on its base Dragonmark, deepening its magic and manifesting unique abilities. Every Greater Mark grants Greater Spellcasting; the abilities that follow it are specific to each Mark.
