docs.text:
5th-Level Evocation

Classes Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 120 ft. Area Special Target — Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

Choose 1 of the following forms:

Form Wall A flat surface of up to 10 contiguous 10-foot-by-10-foot panels, in any orientation Dome Around all or part of up to a 10-foot-radius Sphere

You conjure a ¼-inch thick barrier of magical force in the chosen form.

The barrier has the following effects:

Effect Invisible The barrier is Invisible. Immovable The barrier is Anchored. Impervious The barrier has Immunity to all damage and can't be dispelled. Impassable Nothing can pass through the barrier, including Attacks and other effects. Ward Travel The barrier blocks teleportation and travel through the Ethereal Plane. Ward Targeting A magical effect can't target anything in the area from outside the barrier. Ward Area The area is excluded from every magical effect's area.

Before the barrier appears, you propel each Creature and Object in the barrier's space to either side of it.

docs.title: Wall of Stone
docs.text:
5th-Level Evocation

Classes Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 120 ft. Area Special Target — Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

You conjure a 6-inch thick barrier of nonmagical stone that must merge with and be supported by existing stone. The barrier is a flat surface of 10 contiguous 10-foot-by-10-foot panels, in any orientation.

Before the barrier appears, you propel each Creature and Object in the barrier's space to either side of it. Then, each target in the area makes a Reflex Save.

Fail No effect. Success The target can move up to half its Speed.

Each panel is an Object with Armor Class 15 and 150 Hit Points.

A panel with 0 Hit Points is destroyed, possibly collapsing the panels connected to it.

docs.title: Permanence
docs.text: If this Spell lasts the full duration, the barrier becomes permanent.

docs.title: Arcane Gate
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range 500 ft. Area 2 5-ft. radius Circles Target — Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

You conjure a portal in each area. Each portal is an opaque ring of mist, hovering just above the ground in any orientation.

A portal is open on one side only. Anything that enters the open side of one portal exits from the open side of the other.

docs.title: Turn Portals
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can change which side of each portal is open.

docs.title: Blade Barrier
docs.text:
6th-Level Evocation

Classes Cleric Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range 90 ft. Area A 100-ft. × 5-ft. × 20-ft. Wall, or a 30-ft. radius, 20-ft. Cylinder Target Each Creature and Object Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

The area provides Three-Quarters Cover and is Difficult Terrain.

After a target enters the area (including when this Spell is cast), it makes a Reflex Save. After your Turn starts, each target also makes this Saving Throw. A target only makes this Saving Throw once until the start of your next Turn.

Fail You deal 6d10 Force Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: Bubbling Cauldron
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Warlock, Wizard Components V, S, M (a gilded ladle worth 500 Gold) Casting Time Magic Action Range Reach Area — Target — Duration Until dispelled

Choose a Common or Uncommon Potion.

You conjure a Medium cauldron filled with Spellcasting Ability doses of the chosen Potion, and that many empty vials (minimum 1). The cauldron has Immunity to all damage, is Anchored, and disappears with its liquid after 10 minutes or after the last vial is filled.

After the last dose is consumed, this Spell ends. After you cast this Spell again, the previous casting ends.

docs.title: Fill Vial
docs.text: Bonus Action: You or an Ally that can reach the cauldron can fill 1 vial with a dose of the Potion. A filled vial disappears once its Potion is consumed.

docs.title: Chain Lightning
docs.text:
6th-Level Evocation

Classes Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 150 ft. Area — Target 1 Creature or Object, and up to 3 more within 30 ft. of it Duration —

Each target makes a Reflex Save.

Fail You deal 10d8 Lightning Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 1 target per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Circle of Death
docs.text:
6th-Level Necromancy

Classes Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard Components V, S, M (a crushed black pearl worth 500 Gold) Casting Time Magic Action Range 150 ft. Area A 60-ft. radius Sphere Target Each Creature and Object Duration —

Each target makes a Fortitude Save.

Fail You deal 8d8 Necrotic Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 2d8 damage per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Conjure Fey
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Druid Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range 60 ft. Area — Target — Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

You conjure a fey spirit. The spirit is a Large, intangible Object with Immunity to all damage.

You take the following Action as part of casting this Spell.

docs.title: Attack
docs.text:
Bonus Action: You can move or teleport the spirit up to 30 feet, then make a Melee Spell Attack against a Creature or Object within 5 feet of the spirit.

Hit You deal 3d12 + Spellcasting Ability Psychic Damage and frighten the target until the start of your next Turn.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 1d12 damage per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Contingency
docs.text:
6th-Level Abjuration

Classes Wizard Components V, S, M (a gem-encrusted statuette of yourself worth 1,500 Gold) Casting Time 10 minutes Range — Area — Target Self Duration 10 days

Choose a perceivable trigger and a lower-Level Spell that you can cast, that has a Casting Time of a Magic Action or a Bonus Action, and that can target you.

You cast that Spell as part of casting this one, expending both Spell Slots, but the chosen Spell's effect is delayed.

After the trigger occurs, the Spell takes effect (no Concentration required), targeting you, then this Spell ends.

After this Spell's Material Component leaves your space, this Spell ends. After you cast this Spell again, the previous casting ends.

docs.title: Create Undead
docs.text:
6th-Level Necromancy

Classes Cleric, Warlock, Wizard Components V, S, M (one black onyx stone worth 150 Gold per target) Casting Time 1 minute Range 10 ft. Area — Target Up to 3 Humanoid Corpses, or up to 3 Undead you animated Duration 24 hours

You can cast this Spell only at night.

If a target is a Corpse, you animate it as a Ghoul Companion.

If a target is an Undead you animated, it becomes your Companion.

After this Spell ends, each target stops being your Companion but remains animated.

docs.title: Command Undead
docs.text: Bonus Action: You can command any of your Undead companions within 120 feet to move and take any Action available to them. You give the same command to each target.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: When Upcast, each casting animates or controls 4 Ghouls (7th-Level), 5 Ghouls or 2 Ghasts or Wights (8th-Level), or 6 Ghouls, 3 Ghasts or Wights, or 2 Mummies (9th-Level).

docs.title: Disintegrate
docs.text:
6th-Level Transmutation

Classes Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 60 ft. Area — Target 1 Creature or Object Duration —

If a target is an Object, you disintegrate it, even if it has Immunity to all damage. You disintegrate only a 10-foot Cube of a Huge or larger Object, and you disintegrate an Object conjured by a Spell only if that Spell's Level is no higher than this Spell's.

If a target is a Creature, it makes a Reflex Save.

Fail You deal 10d6 + 40 Force Damage. If the target has 0 Hit Points, it and everything nonmagical it wears and carries are disintegrated into dust, and it can't be resurrected by a lower-Level Spell. Success No effect.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 3d6 damage per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Eyebite
docs.text:
6th-Level Necromancy

Classes Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range — Area — Target Self Duration 1 minute (Concentration)

You take the following Action as part of casting this Spell.

docs.title: Glare
docs.text:
Magic Action: You can choose 1 Creature within 60 feet. The target makes a Will Save.

Fail Choose 1 of the following effects. Success The target gains Immunity to this casting of this Spell. Effect Asleep You put the target to Sleep. Panicked You frighten the target. After a target Frightened by you starts its Turn, it Dashes and moves away from you by the safest route.After a Frightened target ends its Turn at least 60 feet from you where it can't see you, its Fear ends. Sickened You sicken the target.

docs.title: Find the Path
docs.text:
6th-Level Divination

Classes Bard, Cleric, Druid Components V, S, M (divination tools worth 100 Gold, such as cards or runes) Casting Time 1 minute Range The same Plane Area — Target 1 Location you are familiar with Duration 24 hours (Concentration)

You gain the following effects:

  • You know the direction and distance to the target.
  • If the target is moving, you know the direction of its movement.
  • At each choice of paths, you know which is the most direct route to the target.

docs.title: Flesh to Stone
docs.text:
6th-Level Transmutation

Classes Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 60 ft. Area — Target 1 non-Construct Creature Duration 1 minute (Concentration)

Each target makes a Fortitude Save.

Fail You restrain the target. Success The target's Speed becomes 0 feet until the start of your next Turn.

Before a target's Turn ends, it makes a Fortitude Save.

After it fails 3 Saving Throws against this Spell, you petrify it. After it succeeds on 3, this Spell ends on that target.

docs.title: Permanence
docs.text: If this Spell lasts the full duration, the effect lasts until dispelled (no Concentration required).

docs.title: Forbiddance
docs.text:
6th-Level Abjuration

Classes Cleric Components V, S, M (ruby dust worth 1,000 Gold) Casting Time 10 minutes, or Ritual Range Reach Area Up to a 200-ft. Cube Target Each Creature Duration 24 hours

Choose 1 or more Planar Creature Types. The chosen Creature Types become sealed.

Choose Radiant or Necrotic Damage.

The area gains the following effects:

Effect Punish Intruder After a sealed target enters the area (including when this Spell is cast), you deal 5d10 of the chosen Damage Type. After your Turn starts, you deal this damage to each sealed target in the area. You only deal this damage to a target once until the start of your next Turn. Ward Travel Nothing can enter or leave the area by teleportation or Planar Travel.

docs.title: Password
docs.text: After you cast this Spell, you can choose a password. After a creature speaks this password, or presents it visually, the creature ignores this Spell's effects.

docs.title: Permanence
docs.text: If you cast this Spell on the same area every day for 30 days, the Material Component is consumed and the effect lasts until dispelled.

docs.title: Freezing Sphere
docs.text:
6th-Level Evocation

Classes Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 300 ft., or Reach Area A 60-ft. radius Sphere Target Each Creature and Object Duration —

If you cast this Spell at Reach, you delay its effect and hold it as a bead. The bead explodes on its own after 1 minute.

Each target makes a Fortitude Save.

Fail You deal 10d6 Cold Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

A body of water in the area freezes 6 inches deep across its surface for 1 minute, and you restrain each target in that area.

docs.title: Escape
docs.text:
Utilize Action: Any Restrained target can make an Athletics Check against your Spell Save DC.

Success This effect ends on the target. Fail No effect.

docs.title: Throw
docs.text: Attack Action: Any creature holding the bead can throw the bead up to 40 feet or hurl it with a Sling (using the Sling's Long Range). Then, this Spell takes effect centered where the bead lands.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 1d6 damage per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Globe of Invulnerability
docs.text:
6th-Level Abjuration

Classes Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range — Area A 10-ft. Aura Target — Duration 1 minute (Concentration)

You conjure a ¼-inch thick barrier of magical force around the area.

The barrier has the following effects:

Effect Invisible The barrier is Invisible. Immovable The barrier is Anchored. Impervious The barrier has Immunity to all damage. Passable The barrier doesn't impede movement. Ward Targeting A lower-Level magical effect can't target anything in the area from outside the barrier. Ward Area The area is excluded from a lower-Level magical effect's area.

docs.title: Guards and Wards
docs.text:
6th-Level Abjuration

Classes Bard, Wizard Components V, S, M (a silver rod worth 10 Gold) Casting Time 1 hour Range Reach Area Up to a 50-ft. Cube Target Each Creature and Object Duration 24 hours

The area gains the following effects. This Spell can't be dispelled by another effect, but each of its effects can; after each of its effects is dispelled, this Spell is dispelled.

Effect Fogged Corridors The corridors in the area gain the effect of Fog Cloud (dispersed fog returns in 10 minutes). At each intersection or branching passage, a target other than you has a 50% chance of believing it is going in the opposite direction from the one it chooses. Locked Doors Doors in the area gain the effect of Arcane Lock, and you can cover up to 10 of them with an illusion of plain wall. Webbed Stairs The stairs in the area gain the effect of Web (destroyed strands regrow in 10 minutes).

The area gains 1 of the following effects:

Effect Dancing Lights 4 corridors in the area gain the effect of Dancing Lights. Gust of Wind 1 corridor or room in the area gains the effect of Gust of Wind. Magic Mouth 2 locations in the area gain the effect of Magic Mouth. Stinking Cloud 2 locations in the area gain the effect of Stinking Cloud (dispersed vapors return in 10 minutes). Suggestion A target entering a 5-foot Square you choose gains the effect of Suggestion.

docs.title: Password
docs.text: After you cast this Spell, you can choose a password. After a creature speaks this password, or presents it visually, the creature ignores this Spell's effects.

docs.title: Permanence
docs.text: If you cast this Spell on the same area every day for 365 days, the effect lasts until dispelled.

docs.title: Harm
docs.text:
6th-Level Necromancy

Classes Cleric Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range 60 ft. Area — Target 1 Creature Duration —

Each target makes a Fortitude Save.

Fail You deal 14d6 Necrotic Damage, and the target's Hit Point Maximum decreases by that amount. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: Heal
docs.text:
6th-Level Abjuration

Classes Cleric, Druid Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range 60 ft. Area — Target 1 Creature Duration —

You heal each target by 70, and end each Blindness, Deafness, and Sickness on it.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 10 to the healing per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Heroes' Feast
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Bard, Cleric, Druid Components V, S, M (consumes a gem-encrusted bowl worth 1,000 Gold) Casting Time 10 minutes Range Reach Area A 10-ft. Cube Target Up to 12 Creatures Duration 24 hours

You conjure a feast in the area. The feast takes 1 hour to consume, then disappears.

After a target partakes of the feast, it gains the following effects:

  • It gains Poison Resistance.
  • It gains Fear and Sickness Immunity.
  • Its Hit Point Maximum increases by 2d10 and heals by that much.

docs.title: Instant Summons
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Wizard Components V, S, M (a sapphire worth 1,000 Gold) Casting Time 1 minute, or Ritual Range Reach Area — Target 1 Object that weighs 10 pounds or less Duration Until dispelled

You link each target to the Material Component. Each casting requires a different Material Component.

docs.title: Summon
docs.text: Utilize Action: Any creature holding the Material Component can crush it, ending this Spell. Each target teleports to the creature's hand.

docs.title: Irresistible Dance
docs.text:
6th-Level Enchantment

Classes Bard, Wizard Components V Casting Time Magic Action Range 30 ft. Area — Target 1 Creature Duration 1 minute (Concentration)

Each target makes a Will Save.

Fail You charm and immobilize the target. While Charmed by this Spell, a target gains Disadvantage on Attack Rolls, and creatures gain Advantage on Attack Rolls against it. Success You immobilize the target until the end of its next Turn.

docs.title: Break Free
docs.text:
Magic Action: Any Immobilized target can repeat this Saving Throw.

Fail No additional effect. Success This Spell ends on the target.

docs.title: Magic Jar
docs.text:
6th-Level Necromancy

Classes Wizard Components V, S, M (a gem, crystal, or reliquary worth 500 Gold) Casting Time 1 minute Range — Area — Target Self Duration Until dispelled

Your soul leaves your body and enters the Material Component, which becomes its container. While your soul is elsewhere, your body is Incapacitated.

While your soul is in the container, you sense your surroundings from the container's space, and you can't Move or take Reactions.

Your soul returns to your body after the container is destroyed or this Spell ends; if your body is dead or more than 100 feet away, you die instead. If another creature's soul is in the container when it is destroyed, that soul returns to its body if the body is alive and within 100 feet; otherwise, that creature dies.

After your soul returns to your body or you die, this Spell ends. The container is destroyed when this Spell ends.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Magic Action: You can project your soul up to 100 feet from the container, either returning to your body or possessing one Humanoid. A creature warded by Protection from Good & Evil or Magic Circle can't be possessed.

The Humanoid makes a Will Save.

Fail Your soul enters the target's body and you control it, and its soul becomes trapped in the container, where it perceives with its own senses but is Incapacitated. Your Hit Points, Hit Dice, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Speed, and Senses are replaced by the target's; you keep your other statistics. Success You can't attempt to possess the target again for 24 hours.

docs.title: Withdraw
docs.text:
Magic Action: While possessing a body, you can return to the container if it is within 100 feet, returning the host's soul to its body.

If the host body dies while you possess it, the host dies and you make a Will Save against your Spell Save DC. On a success, you return to the container if it is within 100 feet; otherwise, you die.

docs.title: Mass Suggestion
docs.text:
6th-Level Enchantment

Classes Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 60 ft. Area — Target Up to 12 Creatures who understand you Duration 24 hours

Each target gains the effect of Suggestion (you suggest the same activity for each target).

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: When Upcast, the duration is 10 days (7th-Level), 30 days (8th-Level), or 366 days (9th-Level).

docs.title: Move Earth
docs.text:
6th-Level Transmutation

Classes Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 120 ft. Area Up to a 40-ft. Cube Target — Duration 2 hours (Concentration)

You transform dirt, sand, and clay in the area however you choose: raising or lowering its elevation, digging or filling a trench, or raising or flattening a wall or pillar.

No change can exceed half the area's largest dimension, and each takes 10 minutes to complete. The transformation is slow enough that it doesn't trap or injure creatures in the area.

This Spell can't affect natural stone or stone construction, and moved earth carries its plants along with it. Rocks and structures shift to accommodate the new terrain, and an unstable structure might collapse.

After every 10 minutes, you can choose a new area.

docs.title: Planar Ally
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Cleric Components V, S Casting Time 10 minutes Range 60 ft. Area — Target — Duration —

You beseech an otherworldly entity, which sends a Planar Creature loyal to it. You can request a specific creature by name, though the DM decides which one answers.

The creature teleports to you, and is Independent and under no compulsion to serve you. You must be able to communicate with it to bargain for a task, which it performs in exchange for payment.

Task Length Payment Minutes 100 Gold per minute Hours 1,000 Gold per hour Days (up to 10) 10,000 Gold per day

The DM adjusts the payment for the task's danger, and creatures rarely accept a task that seems suicidal.

After the creature completes its task, its agreed service ends, or you can't agree on a price, the creature teleports back to its home plane.

docs.title: Programmed Illusion
docs.text:
6th-Level Illusion

Classes Bard, Wizard Components V, S, M (jade dust worth 25 Gold) Casting Time Magic Action Range 120 ft. Area A 30-ft. Cube Target — Duration Until dispelled

You conjure the image of an object, creature, or other visible phenomenon in the area, describing how it behaves and what sounds it makes for up to 5 minutes. You also specify a trigger, based on visual or audible phenomena occurring within 30 feet of the area.

After the trigger occurs, the image performs as you described, then vanishes and lies dormant for 10 minutes before it can be triggered again.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
A creature whose Passive Perception exceeds your Spell Save DC knows the illusion is false.

Search Action: Any creature that perceives the illusion can make a Perception Check against your Spell Save DC.

Success The creature knows the illusion is false and ignores its effects. Fail No effect.

docs.title: Summon Fiend
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Warlock, Wizard Components V, S, M (a bloody vial worth 600 Gold) Casting Time Magic Action Range 90 ft. Area — Target — Duration 1 hour (Concentration)

Choose Demon, Devil, or Yugoloth.

You conjure a Fiendish Spirit Companion of the chosen type. After the spirit drops to 0 Hit Points, this Spell ends.

docs.title: Command
docs.text: Free Action: You can command the spirit to move and take any Action available to it.

docs.title: Fiendish Spirit: Demon
docs.text:
Large Fiend, Neutral

Defenses HP 72 [(10 + CON) × Spell Level] Hit Dice 1d10 per Spell Level AC 19 + PB [10 + DEX + Spell Level + PB] Armor Natural (Light) Resistance Fire Immunity Poison Protection Magic Condition Immunity Sickness Abilities STR +1 DEX +3 CON +2 INT +0 WIS +0 CHA +3 Traits Languages Abyssal; Understands the Languages you know Senses Darkvision (60 ft.) Speed 40 ft., Climb 40 ft. Reach 5 ft. Features Death Throes After the Spell ends, the spirit explodes. Everything in a 10-foot Aura makes a Reflex Save (DC Spell Save DC); on a failure, you deal 2d10 + Spell Level Fire Damage, or half as much on a success. Multiattack The spirit makes Spell Level ÷ 2 attacks, rounded down.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Bite Melee Attack Range Reach Attack +Spell Attack to hit Damage 1d12 + 9 Necrotic Damage [1d12 + DEX + Spell Level]

docs.title: Fiendish Spirit: Devil
docs.text:
Large Fiend, Neutral

Defenses HP 60 [(8 + CON) × Spell Level] Hit Dice 1d8 per Spell Level AC 19 + PB [10 + DEX + Spell Level + PB] Armor Natural (Light) Resistance Fire Immunity Poison Protection Magic Condition Immunity Sickness Abilities STR +1 DEX +3 CON +2 INT +0 WIS +0 CHA +3 Traits Languages Infernal; Understands the Languages you know Senses Devil's Sight (60 ft.) Speed 40 ft., Fly 60 ft. Reach 5 ft. Features Multiattack The spirit makes Spell Level ÷ 2 attacks, rounded down.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Fiery Strike Melee or Ranged Attack Range Reach or 150 ft. Attack +Spell Attack to hit Damage 2d6 + 9 Fire Damage [2d6 + DEX + Spell Level]

docs.title: Fiendish Spirit: Yugoloth
docs.text:
Large Fiend, Neutral

Defenses HP 84 [(12 + CON) × Spell Level] Hit Dice 1d12 per Spell Level AC 19 + PB [10 + DEX + Spell Level + PB] Armor Natural (Light) Resistance Fire Immunity Poison Protection Magic Condition Immunity Sickness Abilities STR +1 DEX +3 CON +2 INT +0 WIS +0 CHA +3 Traits Languages Telepathy (60 ft.); Understands the Languages you know Senses Darkvision (60 ft.) Speed 40 ft. Reach 5 ft. Features Multiattack The spirit makes Spell Level ÷ 2 attacks, rounded down.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Claws Melee Attack Range Reach Attack +Spell Attack to hit Damage 1d8 + 9 Slashing Damage [1d8 + DEX + Spell Level] Effect After this attack, the spirit can teleport up to 30 feet.

docs.title: Sunbeam
docs.text:
6th-Level Evocation

Classes Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range — Area — Target Self Duration 1 minute (Concentration)

You emit Bright Sunlight out to 30 feet and Dim Sunlight 30 feet further.

You take the following Action as part of casting this Spell.

docs.title: Beam
docs.text:
Magic Action: You can choose a 60-foot × 5-foot Line originating from you. Each Creature and Object in it makes a Fortitude Save.

Fail You deal 6d8 Radiant Damage and blind the target until the start of your next Turn. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: Transport via Plants
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Druid Components V, S Casting Time Magic Action Range 10 ft. Area — Target 1 Large or larger Plant Object Duration 10 minutes

You link each target to another Plant Object on the same plane at any distance, which you have seen or touched before.

docs.title: Step Through
docs.text: Free Action; 5 feet of movement: Any creature that can reach a linked plant can step into the plant and exit from the other.

docs.title: True Seeing
docs.text:
6th-Level Divination

Classes Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard Components V, S, M (consumes mushroom powder worth 25 Gold) Casting Time Magic Action Range Reach Area — Target 1 Creature Duration 1 hour

Each target gains 120 feet of Truesight.

docs.title: Wall of Ice
docs.text:
6th-Level Evocation

Classes Wizard Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 120 ft. Area Special Target — Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

Choose 1 of the following forms:

Form Wall A flat surface of up to 10 contiguous 10-foot-by-10-foot panels, in any orientation Dome All or part of up to a 10-foot-radius Sphere (the barrier is a single panel)

You conjure a 1-foot thick barrier of ice on a solid surface in the chosen form.

Before the barrier appears, you propel each Creature and Object in the barrier's space to either side of it. Then, each target makes a Reflex Save.

Fail You deal 10d6 Cold Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

Each panel is an Object with Armor Class 12, 30 Hit Points, Cold Immunity, and Fire Vulnerability.

A panel with 0 Hit Points is destroyed, leaving a sheet of frigid air in its space. After a target enters the frigid air, it makes a Fortitude Save. After your Turn starts, each target in the frigid air also makes this Saving Throw. A target only makes this Saving Throw once until the start of your next Turn.

Fail You deal 5d6 Cold Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 2d6 damage when the barrier appears and 1d6 damage from the frigid air per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Wall of Thorns
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Druid Components V, S, M Casting Time Magic Action Range 120 ft. Area A 60-ft. × 5-ft. × 10-ft. Wall, or a 10-ft. radius, 20-ft. Cylinder Target Each Creature and Object Duration 10 minutes (Concentration)

The area is Heavily Obscured, and each foot a creature moves through it costs 3 extra feet.

After a target enters the area (including when this Spell is cast), it makes a Reflex Save. After your Turn starts, each target in the area also makes this Saving Throw. A target only makes this Saving Throw once until the start of your next Turn.

Fail You deal 7d8 Piercing Damage. Success You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 1d8 damage per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Wind Walk
docs.text:
6th-Level Transmutation

Classes Druid Components V, S, M Casting Time 1 minute Range 30 ft. Area — Target You and up to 10 Allies Duration 8 hours

Each target gains the effect of Gaseous Form (it gains a 300-foot Hover Speed instead).

After this Spell ends, a falling target gains the effect of Feather Fall.

docs.title: Change Form
docs.text: Utilize Action: Any target can stun itself for 1 minute. Then, it loses or regains the effect of Gaseous Form.

docs.title: Word of Recall
docs.text:
6th-Level Conjuration

Classes Cleric Components V Casting Time Magic Action Range 5 ft. Area — Target You and up to 5 Allies Duration —

Choose 1 of the following effects:

Effect Designate Your current location becomes your Recall Sanctuary, provided it qualifies. Recall Each target teleports to your Recall Sanctuary, appearing in the nearest unoccupied spaces to the spot you designated. If you don't have a Recall Sanctuary, this effect does nothing.

docs.title: Recall Sanctuaries
docs.text: Any Location dedicated to or strongly linked to a deity you worship, such as a temple or shrine, can become a Recall Sanctuary. You can have only one Recall Sanctuary at a time.

docs.title: Spelljammer Schematic
docs.text: Spelljamming is the art of sailing magical ships across the void between worlds.

docs.title: Gravity
docs.text:
There are three types of Gravity:

Gravity Description Gravity Naturally occurring phenomena that pulls you toward the center of sufficiently large masses, such as planetoids and some Leviathans. Gravity Plane Artificial, magical gravity produced by Spelljamming ships. Instead of pulling toward the center, gravity planes pull toward a horizontal plane, usually bisecting the ship. Microgravity Naturally occurring gravity produced by Small and larger creatures and objects. Microgravity has a minuscule effect that keeps objects within your space from floating away.

docs.title: Moving in Zero-Gravity
docs.text:
In areas outside of a Gravity or Gravity Plane, creatures can't move unless they gain a Fly Speed, climb or push off of a surface, or are propelled.

After anything without a Hover Speed moves in zero-Gravity, it starts Drifting the same distance and direction (This is effectively half speed unless you're moving in a straight line, since Drifting costs movement to change direction).

docs.title: Atmosphere
docs.text: The Astral Sea is a nearly perfect void, and what little atmosphere exists is not suitable for breathing. When a creature enters this void from an atmosphere, the creature's Microgravity keeps enough air (the same Air Quality as the exited atmosphere) to breathe for a short amount of time. It takes 1 minute for a Microgravity's Fresh Air to degrade to Foul, and a further 3 hours to degrade to Deadly.

docs.title: Exiting Atmosphere
docs.text: Any creature large enough to have Microgravity always has air around them, so transitioning between atmosphere and the void poses no physical risk.

docs.title: Air Envelopes
docs.text:
A Ship that produces a Gravity Plane also holds an Air Envelope, an envelope of air wherever that Gravity reaches. For an appropriately sized crew, it takes 30 days for a Ship's Fresh Air to degrade to Foul, and a further 90 days to degrade to Deadly.

A Ship that doesn't produce a Gravity Plane, or one that loses their Gravity Plane, still holds air within the Ship's natural Microgravity, but it takes only 10 days for the air to degrade to Foul, and a further 30 days to degrade to Deadly.

docs.title: Sealing a Ship
docs.text: Some Ships can be Sealed and pressurized to extend their atmosphere. Such a ship doubles the amount of time before their Air Quality degrades, but must take additional measures to enter and exit the ship without breaking the seal.

docs.title: Depressurization
docs.text:
When a Sealed Ship is breached, it undergoes a Depressurization: the air inside rushes out as the pressure rebalances. The larger the Ship, the more dangerous the breach.

Everything within 20 feet of the breach makes a Reflex Save (no DC).

Each target is propelled 30 - their Save total (rounded down to a multiple of 5) feet in a straight line toward the breach (potentially ending up on the other side).

The range of the breach and the distance each target is propelled are both multiplied by the Ship's Size Class.

docs.title: Ship Encounters
docs.text: Combat between ships is fought Turn by Turn as each crew's Officers steer, fire, and work their magic in Initiative order.

docs.title: Ship Initiative
docs.text:
Ship Encounters begin when a Ship becomes aware of a threat, such as an Enemy Ship or a Leviathan-sized creature. When a Ship rolls Initiative, one of its Officers rolls for it using that Officer's Initiative bonus. The result is shared by the Ship's crew and passengers.

Each Ship in an encounter gets at least one Turn each Round for each Officer aboard it. Ship Turns are taken in Initiative order, alternating between each Ship and choosing a different Officer to act on the Ship's behalf each Turn. A Ship with fewer Officers than another still acts when its Initiative comes up, assigning extra Turns to its Officers as needed.

The Round ends once every Officer has taken at least one Turn and each Ship has taken the same number of Turns. The next Round then begins normally.

docs.title: Ship Actions
docs.text:
On each of a Ship's turns, one of the Ship's Officers are chosen to take an Action on the Ship's behalf. Each Officer has a different set of Ship Actions available to them.

A character without an Officer role acts as a passenger or crew and doesn't take Turns during Ship Combat.

Most of an adventurer's normal features are ineffective at the scale Ships operate. Even so, an Officer can spend their Ship Action to instead take one Normal Action or Bonus Action, or to cast a Spell with a Casting Time of 1 minute or less. Officers keep their Reaction, as normal.

docs.title: Prevented Actions
docs.text: While a Ship is affected by an effect that prevents Actions, such as being Incapacitated, an Officer is still chosen on the Ship's Turns, but that Officer takes no Action.

docs.title: Encounter Scale
docs.text: Time and distance in a Ship Encounter aren't strictly measured in minutes, feet, squares, or tiles; Ships in the astral sea travel vast distances, and move faster than ships their size could in atmosphere.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: Time during Ship Combat is tracked in Rounds, which can be as quick as a few seconds or as long as a few minutes. For resolving creature-scale effects, treat 1 Round as 1 minute. The longer timescale reflects the rhythm of ship-to-ship engagements, where movement and coordination matter more than split-second reactions.

docs.title: Distance
docs.text:
The distance between Ships is tracked in four broad Engagement Ranges: Close, Long, Extreme, and Retreat. Most encounters begin at Extreme range, where combatants are aware of one another but can't yet effectively target each other with shipboard Weapons.

Engagement Range Description Close Point-blank engagement. Combat here is risky, since escape isn't always an option. Long The distance most Ships prefer to engage at, unless they are built for Close-range combat. Extreme Where most encounters open, beyond the effective reach of shipboard Weapons. Retreat Beyond Extreme range. At the end of each Round, a Ship at Retreat range from all its Enemies escapes the combat.

An ordinary creature's Attacks rarely reach beyond Close range and matter little until boarding occurs.

docs.title: Damage
docs.text: Ships endure far more damage than individual creatures, and their Weapons strike accordingly. Damage dealt to a Ship from a non-Ship source is halved, and damage dealt by a Ship to a non-Ship is doubled.

docs.title: Leviathans
docs.text:
Leviathans are colossal creatures of the void so vast they're treated as ships, fighting with their own Actions rather than a crew.

A Leviathan follows the same rules as a Ship and is treated as one.

docs.title: Leviathan Actions
docs.text:
Instead of Officers, a Leviathan has a set number of Actions it takes each Round. On each of its Turns, it takes one of those Actions, just as a Ship would, and typically can't take that Action again in the same Round.

If a Leviathan uses an ability that takes multiple Actions to complete, it spends each of its Turns Concentrating on that ability. It can't act again until the final required Turn, when the ability resolves.

docs.title: Creating a Ship
docs.text: This page details building a vessel from the ground up, choosing its size, hull, defenses, and the components its crew will command.

docs.title: Ship Size
docs.text: A Ship's size is measured by its length and width, in feet. For every 30 feet of the Ship's longest dimension (rounded up), its Size Class increases by 1.

docs.title: Size Penalty
docs.text: Before a Ship's Pilot makes a Piloting Check, reduce the total by the Ship's Size Class. This reduction is the Ship's Size Penalty.

docs.title: Ram Damage
docs.text: Whenever a Ship's Pilot uses the Ram Action, its Ram Damage adds 2d10 Bludgeoning Damage for each point of Size Class the Ship has.

docs.title: Hull Material
docs.text:
Most Ships are made from Wood or an equivalent substance. Alternative materials can affect a Ship's defenses and mobility.

In progress

Ship Materials are currently factored in to the base ship stats. A future update will describe the precise effect a material has on the ship.

docs.title: Defenses
docs.text: A Ship's defensive capability is measured by its Armor Class, Damage Threshold, Hull Points, and Keel Points.

docs.title: Hull Points
docs.text: Hull Points (HP) represent a Ship's external defenses and can be repaired readily, even during combat. When a Ship's Hull Points reach 0, it is Incapacitated but not destroyed. It can then be boarded, and its Keel Points can be targeted.

docs.title: Keel Points
docs.text: Keel Points (KP) represent a Ship's structural integrity. A Ship has far fewer Keel Points, and they can't be restored without powerful magic or extensive downtime. When a Ship's Keel Points reach 0, the Ship is destroyed, its life support fails, and its crew are in mortal danger.

docs.title: Ship Bases
docs.text:
Ship Bases are the framework for Astral Sea vessels, each with its own stat block, strengths, and role in a fleet.

A Ship's stat block lists its size, maneuverability, hull, and capacity for Components. Some Ships come with specific Components already installed; these don't count against the Ship's Component limits.

docs.title: Sailing Ship
docs.text: Defenses HP 250 KP 50 AC 15 DT 15 Material Wood Ram Damage 8d10 Size 120 × 20 ft. Size Penalty 4 Components Pilot 2 Quartermaster 4 Spelljammer 1

docs.title: Wasp
docs.text: Defenses HP 250 KP 50 AC 17 DT 15 Material Wood Ram Damage 8d10 Size 80 × 20 ft. Size Penalty 2 Components Pilot 2 Quartermaster 2 Spelljammer 1

docs.title: Hammerhead
docs.text: Defenses HP 350 KP 70 AC 15 DT 15 Material Wood Ram Damage 16d10 Size 240 × 25 ft. Size Penalty 8 Components Pilot 2 Quartermaster 3 Spelljammer 1

docs.title: Naval Ram
docs.text:
Pilot Component

Defenses HP 100 KP 20 AC 20 DT 10

Whenever you Ram, you gain Advantage on your Piloting check, and this Ram takes the damage instead of your hull.

docs.title: Skyliner
docs.text: Defenses HP 50 KP 10 AC 19 DT 10 Material Metal Ram Damage 2d10 Size 10 × 5 ft. Size Penalty 0 Features Personal This Ship's Pilot can also be its Spelljammer. The Pilot's and Spelljammer's Turns are still separate. Components Pilot 1 Quartermaster — Spelljammer 1

docs.title: Ship Components
docs.text: Ship Components are the installed systems that expand what a ship can do, each tied to one of its Officers and the role they command.

docs.title: Components in Combat
docs.text: Components that have their own Armor Class and Hull Points can be attacked, just as a Ship's hull is. A Component without combat statistics can't be attacked.

docs.title: Disabling Components
docs.text: When a Component's Hull Points reach 0, it is Disabled. A Disabled Component offers no effects, can't be used, and can't be easily repaired in combat.

docs.title: Destroying Components
docs.text: When a Component's Keel Points reach 0, it is destroyed. A destroyed Component is irreparably damaged and must be replaced outside of combat.

docs.title: Pilot Components
docs.text: Pilot Components are the systems that enhance a ship's movement, giving the Pilot new ways to maneuver and outrun a foe.

docs.title: Afterburners
docs.text:
Pilot Component

One use per Combat

After you Advance or Retreat, you can immediately Advance, Retreat, or Ram.

docs.title: Hunter's Sails
docs.text:
Pilot Component

Whenever you advance, you gain Advantage on your Piloting check.

docs.title: Mirage Sails
docs.text:
Pilot Component

After you Retreat, creatures gain Disadvantage on Attacks against your Ship until the Pilot's next Turn.

docs.title: Naval Ram
docs.text:
Pilot Component

Defenses HP 100 KP 20 AC 20 DT 10

Whenever you Ram, you gain Advantage on your Piloting check, and this Ram takes the damage instead of your hull.

docs.title: Wake Breakers
docs.text:
Pilot Component

Other Ships gain Disadvantage on Piloting checks to advance into, or retreat out of, Close range.

docs.title: Quartermaster Components
docs.text: Quartermaster Components are the weapons and systems the crew operates, expanding the orders a Quartermaster can give in battle.

docs.title: Ballista
docs.text:
Quartermaster Weapon

Defenses HP 50 KP 10 AC 15 DT — Range Attack Damage Close / Long +4 to hit 3d10 Piercing

docs.title: Cannon
docs.text:
Quartermaster Weapon

Defenses HP 100 KP 20 AC 17 DT — Range Attack Damage Long +6 to hit 5d10 Bludgeoning

docs.title: Carronade
docs.text:
Quartermaster Weapon

Defenses HP 100 KP 20 AC 17 DT — Range Attack Damage Close +6 to hit 5d10 Bludgeoning

docs.title: Dragon Figurehead
docs.text:
Quartermaster Weapon

Defenses HP 100 KP 20 AC 15 DT 10 Range Attack Damage Close +4 to hit 8d6 Fire

This Weapon deals half damage on a miss, ignoring Damage Thresholds.

docs.title: Harpoon
docs.text:
Quartermaster Weapon

Defenses HP 50 KP 10 AC 15 DT — Range Attack Damage Close +5 to hit 2d10 Piercing

This Weapon Grapples its target and can't be fired again until the target is freed. Attacks against a Grappled Ship gain Advantage. If a Grappled Ship retreats successfully, it doesn't move and the Grapple ends.

docs.title: Howitzer
docs.text:
Quartermaster Weapon

Defenses HP 250 KP 50 AC 19 DT — Range Attack Damage Long +5 to hit 16d10 Bludgeoning

This Weapon requires two orders to fire.

docs.title: Living Hull
docs.text:
Quartermaster Component

After the Quartermaster starts their Turn, the hull heals 10 Hull Points.

Each Day, the hull heals 1 Keel Point.

docs.title: Reinforced Hull
docs.text:
Quartermaster Component

Your hull's Hull Point maximum is doubled.

docs.title: Spelljammer Helms
docs.text: Spelljammer Helms are the magical seats that power a ship, each inscribed with the Jamming Protocols a Spelljammer can call upon.

docs.title: Artillerist's Helm
docs.text:
Spelljammer Helm

Protocols Eldritch Blaster, Targeting System, Warding Field, plus 2 others.

Your Protocols that target at Close range can also target at Long range.

docs.title: Resonance Helm
docs.text:
Spelljammer Helm

Protocols Eldritch Blaster, Targeting System, Warding Field, plus 2 others.

You can Concentrate on an additional Protocol. You make each Concentration Save separately.

docs.title: Righteous Helm
docs.text:
Spelljammer Helm

Protocols Eldritch Blaster, Targeting System, Warding Field, plus 2 others.

Before your Ship deals Damage, you can expend a Spell Slot to deal an additional 1d10 Radiant Damage, plus 1d10 for each Level of the Spell Slot expended.

docs.title: Standard Helm
docs.text:
Spelljammer Helm

Protocols Eldritch Blaster, Targeting System, Warding Field, plus 3 others.

docs.title: Warden's Helm
docs.text:
Spelljammer Helm

Protocols Eldritch Blaster, Targeting System, Warding Field, plus 2 others.

Your Warding Field also increases your Ship's Damage Threshold.

docs.title: Officers
docs.text: A ship's Officers are the crew members who command it in battle, each taking charge of a different part of the vessel. A ship runs on its Pilot, Quartermaster, and Spelljammer.

docs.title: Changing Roles
docs.text:
Officer roles are chosen before combat begins and usually don't change during an encounter, though they can shift mid-combat if circumstances demand.

An Officer can spend their Ship Action to take over another Officer's role if that Officer consents or is Incapacitated.

When an Officer role becomes vacant — either because its occupant switched roles or can no longer perform their duties — any character without an Officer role can assume the vacant role immediately (no action required).

docs.title: Pilot
docs.text:
The Pilot steers the ship, jockeying for position and driving it through daring maneuvers to overtake the enemy.

Pilots have three Pilot Actions available, plus Pilot Maneuvers that enhance those Actions by expending Maneuver Dice. A Pilot begins each combat with 2 × Proficiency Bonus d6 Maneuver Dice.

docs.title: Piloting Checks
docs.text: Some Pilot Actions require a Piloting Check, usually contested by an Enemy Ship's Pilot. A Piloting check uses your Precision proficiency with your choice of Strength or Dexterity.

docs.title: Size Class
docs.text:
Every Ship has a Size Class that reduces the total of your Piloting Checks and adds damage to your Ram Action.

Pilot Action Description Advance / Retreat Maneuver closer to or farther from an Enemy Ship. Hold Steady Keep your Ship's path as steady as possible. Ram Collide with an Enemy Ship.

docs.title: Advance / Retreat
docs.text:
You make a Piloting check against an Enemy Ship.

Success You move one range closer or farther.

docs.title: Hold Steady
docs.text: Until your next Turn, your Ship gains Advantage on Attacks, but creatures also gain Advantage on Attacks against your Ship.

docs.title: Ram
docs.text:
You make a Piloting check against an Enemy Ship within Close range.

Success You roll 2 × your Size Class d10s and deal the total as Bludgeoning Damage to the Enemy Ship's hull, and half as much to your own hull. Failure Until your next Turn, creatures gain Advantage on Attacks against your Ship.

docs.title: Pilot Maneuvers
docs.text:
A Pilot learns Maneuvers based on their Class Levels. You can use a Maneuver only when its condition is met, provided you expend one of your Maneuver Dice to do so.

Whenever a Pilot Maneuver refers to a Ship's AC, or to Attacks made against a Ship, this means the AC of the hull as well as all the Ship's Weapons.

docs.title: Level 1 Maneuvers
docs.text: Maneuver Artificer Barbarian Fighter Monk Paladin Ranger Rogue Barrel Roll ✓ ✓ ✓ Parting Shot ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Punch It ✓ ✓ Ride the Current ✓ ✓ ✓ Rolling Scissors ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓

docs.title: Barrel Roll
docs.text:
Class List Level 1 Fighter, Monk, or Rogue Trigger Free Action, before an Enemy Advances or Rams Duration —

Add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check.

Success You cause the Enemy to overshoot and move one range farther from you.

docs.title: Parting Shot
docs.text:
Class List Level 1 Fighter, Paladin, Ranger, or Rogue Trigger Reaction, after you or an Enemy Retreats Duration Until the end of your next Turn

Add a Maneuver Die to your Ship's Attack Rolls.

docs.title: Punch It
docs.text:

Add a Maneuver Die to the Initiative check, and to your Ship's AC and Attack Rolls.

docs.title: Ride the Current
docs.text:

Add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check.

Success You move an additional range.

docs.title: Rolling Scissors
docs.text:
Class List Level 1 Artificer, Barbarian, Fighter, or Paladin Trigger Reaction, after an Enemy Advances Duration Until the end of your next Turn

Subtract a Maneuver Die from the damage your Ship takes.

docs.title: Collision Course
docs.text:
Class List Level 5 Barbarian, Fighter, Paladin, or Rogue Trigger Reaction, after an Enemy advances to Close range Duration —

You Ram the Enemy and add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check. If you fail, Attacks against your Ship don't gain Advantage.

docs.title: High Loop
docs.text:
Class List Level 5 Artificer, Monk, Ranger, or Rogue Trigger Free Action, before you Advance Duration —

Add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check.

Success Add that die's result to your Ship's Damage Rolls until your next Turn.

docs.title: Ironclad
docs.text:
Class List Level 5 Artificer, Barbarian, Fighter, or Paladin Trigger Free Action, after you Hold Steady Duration Until the start of your next Turn

Add a Maneuver Die to your Ship's Damage Rolls and subtract a Maneuver Die from the damage your Ship takes.

docs.title: Serpentine
docs.text:
Class List Level 5 Fighter, Monk, Ranger, or Rogue Trigger Free Action, before you Advance or Retreat Duration —

Add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check.

Success Add that die's result to your Ship's AC until your next Turn.

docs.title: Level 9 Maneuvers
docs.text: Maneuver Artificer Barbarian Fighter Monk Paladin Ranger Rogue Bombing Run ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Evasive Maneuvers ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Locked On ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Ramming Speed ✓ ✓ ✓

docs.title: Bombing Run
docs.text:
Class List Level 9 Artificer, Barbarian, Fighter, Paladin, or Rogue Trigger Free Action, after you Advance to Close range Duration Until the start of your next Turn

Add a Maneuver Die to your Ship's Damage Rolls, and your Ship's Critical Hit range increases by 2.

docs.title: Evasive Maneuvers
docs.text:
Class List Level 9 Fighter, Monk, Ranger, or Rogue Trigger Reaction, before an Enemy Attacks Duration —

You make a Piloting check, adding a Maneuver Die to it. The total is your Ship's AC against the triggering Attack.

Until your next Turn, your Ship gains Resistance to all damage.

docs.title: Locked On
docs.text:
Class List Level 9 Artificer, Monk, Ranger, or Rogue Trigger Free Action, before you Advance Duration Until the start of your next Turn

Add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check.

Success Your Ship gains Advantage on Attacks.

docs.title: Ramming Speed
docs.text:
Class List Level 9 Barbarian, Fighter, or Paladin Trigger Free Action, before you Ram Duration —

Add a Maneuver Die to your Piloting check.

Success Your Ship takes half damage from the Ram. If you succeed by 5 or more, each Enemy Officer is Incapacitated until the end of their next Turn.

docs.title: Quartermaster
docs.text:
The Quartermaster directs the crew, calling out orders that ready the ship's hull, weapons, and systems for the fight.

The Quartermaster can use their Ship Action to issue a number of orders up to their Proficiency Bonus. Each order targets a specific part of the Ship, and you can issue the same order more than once.

docs.title: Brace for Impact!
docs.text: Until your next Turn, your hull's Damage Threshold increases by 5.

docs.title: Damage Control!
docs.text: The hull heals 6d6 Hull Points.

docs.title: Trim the Sails!
docs.text: Until your next Turn, the Pilot can use one Pilot Maneuver that requires a Reaction without expending their Reaction.

docs.title: Lay the Lines!
docs.text: Until your next Turn, the Spelljammer can reroll one die rolled as part of a Jamming Protocol or Concentration Save.

docs.title: Open Fire!
docs.text:
You attack with a Weapon, targeting an Enemy Ship's hull or one of its Components.

Whenever you attack with a Ship Weapon, you can use any Ability, provided you can explain how it helps you or your crew hit. Add the chosen Ability and the Weapon's fixed Attack bonus to the Attack Roll. You add nothing to the Damage Roll.

docs.title: Damage Control!
docs.text: The Weapon heals 6d6 Hull Points.

docs.title: Component Orders
docs.text: If a Ship Component has Hull Points or an activatable effect, you can target it with these Orders.

docs.title: Activate!
docs.text: You use an effect listed in the Component's description.

docs.title: Damage Control!
docs.text: The Component heals 6d6 Hull Points.

docs.title: Spelljammer
docs.text:
The Spelljammer sits at the ship's Helm and channels Spell Slots into Protocols, spell-like powers that drive and defend the ship.

While seated in the Ship's spelljamming Helm, the Spelljammer can expend Spell Slots to use Protocols — spell-like effects amplified for Ship Combat.

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text:
Protocols behave like Spells, except they need no Components. A Jamming Protocol uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as its Spellcasting Ability.

Whenever a Protocol refers to a Ship's AC, or to Attacks made against a Ship, this includes the AC of the hull as well as all the Ship's Weapons and Components.

docs.title: Casting Protocols
docs.text: Each spelljamming Helm comes with a set of inscribed Protocols. You can also use a Protocol that isn't inscribed in the Helm, provided you can cast the Protocol's base Spell.

docs.title: Concentration
docs.text: While Concentrating on a Protocol, whenever the Ship's hull takes damage, you make a Concentration Save as though you took the damage. Your Concentration ends if you or the Ship are Incapacitated, or if you aren't seated in the Helm.

docs.title: Aether Cannon
docs.text:
5th-Level Evocation

Base Spell Fireball Activation Time Ship Action Range Close or Long Target A Ship Duration —

You make a Ranged Spell Attack against the target.

Hit You deal 12d10 Force Damage. Miss You deal half as much damage.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 2d10 damage per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Air Envelope
docs.text:
2nd-Level Abjuration

Your Ship's Air Quality becomes Fresh.

docs.text: Double the duration per additional Spell Level.

docs.text:

Your Ship's microgravity fills with darkness. Darkvision can't see through it, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

docs.title: Cloaking Device
docs.text:
4th-Level Illusion

Your Ship turns Invisible. This Protocol ends if your Ship attacks, deals damage, or uses another Protocol.

Creatures aboard your Ship see a glowing outline around hidden, Invisible, or ethereal Ships and creatures.

docs.text:

You speak a short message aloud.

Each creature that understands language within the plane, color bank, or local region of the astral sea you occupy receives the message telepathically and becomes aware of your current location.

docs.text:
Evocation Cantrip

Base Spell Fire Bolt Activation Time Ship Action Range Close or Long Target A Ship Duration —

You make a Ranged Spell Attack against the target.

Hit You deal 3d10 Force Damage.

docs.text: Add 2d10 Force Damage at Level 5, Level 11, and Level 17.

docs.title: Emergency Repairs
docs.text:
1st-Level Transmutation

Choose your Ship's Hull or one of its Components.

Hull You heal the Hull by 4d8. Component You heal the Component by 2d8. This can restore a Component at 0 Hull Points to working order.

docs.title: At Higher Levels
docs.text: Add 4d8 to the healing or 1 target per additional Spell Level.

docs.title: Phase Drive
docs.text:
3rd-Level Transmutation

Your Ship briefly slips into the Ethereal Plane, avoiding the triggering damage.

docs.title: Shields Up
docs.text:
2nd-Level Abjuration

Base Spell Shield Activation Time Reaction, before your Ship is hit with an Attack Range — Target Self Duration Until the end of your next Turn

Your Ship's Armor Class increases by 5.

docs.title: Targeting System

The next Attack your Ship makes gains Advantage.

Your Ship's Armor Class increases by PB.
